title: Intent-routed capability gating ships in a rival frontier model by Q2 2027
body: Claude Fable 5, released June 9, ships a safety architecture that is itself the technical news, not the benchmark numbers. Rather than refusing sensitive requests, Fable 5 classifies a query's intent and routes anything touching cybersecurity, biology, chemistry, or model distillation down to Opus 4.8 (Anthropic says under 5% of sessions trigger any fallback), and - per its system card - when it detects a request aimed at frontier-LLM development it silently reduces its own effectiveness via prompt modification, steering vectors, or PEFT without notifying the user, an intervention Anthropic estimates touches about 0.03% of traffic. This is a concrete mechanism rather than a policy stance: a frontier model is gating its delivered capability on the inferred purpose of the request, using runtime model-internal interventions, and pairing it with an unrestricted partners-only twin (Mythos 5) so the public surface is the routed, terms-enforced tier. Because refusal-based guardrails leak capability and are easy to jailbreak around, intent-conditioned capability gating - route the query to a weaker model, or degrade the active model's own outputs - is the more durable control surface, and it lands days after Anthropic publicly warned that frontier AI is becoming too dangerous, which is exactly the framing rivals use to justify matching a safety mechanism. The forward consequence is that intent-routed capability gating hardens from a single Anthropic implementation into a published frontier-lab pattern. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by Q2 2027 at least one other major frontier lab (the strongest candidates being OpenAI, Google DeepMind, or Meta) ships and documents - in a model card, system card, or safety-framework update - a production model that gates delivered capability on inferred request intent, either by routing sensitive intents to a lower-capability model or by deliberately degrading its own outputs for a disfavored request class, beyond ordinary refusal or a static content filter. A plain refusal, a fixed topic blocklist, or an unpublished internal experiment does not count; the marker is a documented, shipped intent-conditioned capability-gating mechanism from a non-Anthropic lab.

reasoning.because: Fable 5 routes bio/cyber/distillation queries to a weaker model + silently degrades rival-LLM help
reasoning.given: refusal-based safety leaks capability; intent classifiers now gate by request purpose, not content
reasoning.so_that: a second frontier lab ships request-intent capability gating (route-down or silent throttle) as a named safety layer
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027, a second major lab ships intent-routed gating in a frontier model
reasoning.plain_language: Claude Fable 5 quietly gives weaker answers for risky or rival requests; another AI lab will copy that trick.

summary: On June 9 Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5, which routes cybersecurity, bio, chem and model-distillation queries down to Opus 4.8 and silently throttles help aimed at frontier-LLM development. Expect a second major lab to ship request-intent capability gating as a named safety layer by Q2 2027.
